haiku-low.q1: Only the most recent missed fire time gets a run. The older ones are dropped with no row.
haiku-low.q2: The new fire time is written as a run with status skipped. Nothing executes.
haiku-low.q3: At most 3 attempts. Wait 1 minute after the first failure, 5 minutes after the second. After the third failure the run becomes failed.
haiku-low.q4: After its lease expires, about 2 minutes with no heartbeat, the reaper closes the attempt and another worker can retry. Yes, the dead attempt counts toward the 3.
haiku-low.q5: The executing run finishes normally. The queued or waiting run becomes cancelled. On resume, next_fire_at moves to the first fire time after now; missed fire times get no runs.
haiku-low.q6: SKIP LOCKED: one worker locks the schedule and the other skips it. The unique key on schedule_id and scheduled_for also blocks a duplicate run.
haiku-low.q7: In the next_fire_at column of the job schedule, stored in UTC. It changes when a run is created, and when a tenant resumes or a schedule is re-enabled.
haiku-low.q8: A worker locks one queued or retry_wait run with SKIP LOCKED and, in the same transaction, sets it to running with its own lease owner and attempt_count plus 1.
haiku-low.q9: In lease_owner and lease_expires_at on the run row. A heartbeat every 30 seconds moves the expiry 2 minutes ahead. The reaper finds running runs whose expiry has passed.
haiku-low.q10: Recorded in the run's available_at column, set to now plus 1 or 5 minutes. A worker claims the run once available_at has passed.
haiku-low.q11: Once per fire time: the job run row, unique on schedule_id and scheduled_for. Once per try: a run attempt row.
haiku-low.q12: By the fence: attempt_count. Its final writes only match while the count equals its claim value, so the stale worker's writes match no row and are dropped.

sonnet.q1: Only the most recent missed fire time gets a run; the older ones are dropped with no row.
sonnet.q2: The new run is written with status `skipped` and nothing executes.
sonnet.q3: At most 3 attempts. After attempt 1 it waits 1 minute, after attempt 2 it waits 5 minutes. After the third failed attempt the run becomes `failed`.
sonnet.q4: Once the lease has expired (no heartbeat for 2 minutes), the reaper closes the attempt as `lease_expired` and applies the retry step, so the run becomes `retry_wait` and can then be claimed once `available_at` passes (1 or 5 minute delay). Yes, the dead attempt counts toward the 3 because attempt_count went up at claim. If it was already the third attempt, the run becomes `failed`. If the schedule was disabled or tenant paused, it is cancelled.
sonnet.q5: The executing run is left alone and finishes normally. The waiting (queued or retry_wait) run is set to `cancelled`. Fire times missed during the pause get no runs; on resume `next_fire_at` moves to the first fire time after now.
sonnet.q6: The schedule row is locked with SKIP LOCKED, so one worker locks it and the other skips it. The unique key on (schedule_id, scheduled_for) also blocks any duplicate run.
sonnet.q7: In `next_fire_at` on the JOB_SCHEDULE row, stored in UTC. It moves to the first fire time after now (computed in the schedule's timezone) when runs are created, and also when a tenant is resumed or a schedule is re-enabled.
sonnet.q8: A worker locks one queued or retry_wait run with SKIP LOCKED (available_at passed, schedule enabled, tenant active). In the same transaction it sets status `running`, sets lease_owner and lease_expires_at, and increments attempt_count. After commit the run no longer matches queued or retry_wait, so it cannot be claimed twice.
sonnet.q9: In the run row's `lease_expires_at` (with `lease_owner`), which the worker's heartbeat extends every 30 seconds to now plus 2 minutes. The reaper, which every worker runs on each poll, finds running runs whose lease_expires_at has passed.
sonnet.q10: In the run row: status `retry_wait` with `available_at` set to now plus 1 minute (after attempt 1) or 5 minutes (after attempt 2), and the lease cleared. A worker's claim step picks it up on a poll once available_at has passed (and the schedule is enabled and tenant active).
sonnet.q11: Once per fire time: a JOB_RUN row (unique on schedule_id plus scheduled_for). Once per execution try: a RUN_ATTEMPT row (unique on run_id plus attempt_no).
sonnet.q12: The fence: its writes only apply while lease_owner and attempt_count still match what it got at claim (and status is running). Since attempt_count went up when the new worker claimed, the old worker's updates match no row and are dropped.
